title: Digital–analog perceptual duality.
abstract: Could the abstract ideas of our minds originate from neuronal interactions within our brains? In addressing this long-standing question, we analyze interactions within the "brain-world" (BW) and "brain-brain" (BB) domains, representing the brain's physical interactions with its environment and the mental interactions between brains, respectively. BW interactions are characterized as analog-continuous in time and value-while BB interactions are digital-discrete in time and value. Digital signaling allows BB interactions to facilitate effective, albeit information-limited, communication through categorization. We review existing data showing that cascades of neural loops can convert between analog and digital signals, thereby linking physical and mental processes. Importantly, we show that these circuits cannot reduce one domain to the other nor retrace the underlying transformations, suggesting that the mind-body duality can be mapped onto the BB-BW duality. This mapping, supported by both behavioral and neuronal data, situates the mind-body division at the level of subjective perception and suggests that the mind's foundation is inherently social. Thus, the BWBB scheme offers a novel account of the physical-mental gap, acknowledging the coexistence of the physical body and the nonphysical mind while eliminating the need for a recursive homunculus in the brain or an independent mental foundation in the universe. abstract_zh: 我们心灵中的抽象概念是否可能源于大脑内神经元的相互作用？为解决这一长期存在的问题，我们分析了“脑—世界”（BW）和“脑—脑”（BB）领域内的相互作用，分别代表大脑与其环境之间的物理相互作用以及大脑之间的心理相互作用。BW 相互作用在时间和取值上表现为模拟—连续，而 BB 相互作用在时间和取值上表现为数字—离散。数字信号使 BB 相互作用能够通过分类促进有效（尽管受信息限制）的交流。我们回顾了现有数据，表明神经环流的级联可以在模拟与数字信号之间转换，从而连接物理过程与心理过程。重要的是，我们表明这些电路无法将一个领域还原为另一个领域，也无法重述底层的转换过程，这意味着身心二元性可以映射到 BB–BW 二元性之上。该映射由行为学和神经元数据支持，将身心的区分置于主观感知的层面，并表明心灵的基础本质上是社会性的。因此，BWBB 方案对物理—精神差距提供了一种新的解释，既承认物理身体与非物理心灵的共存，又消除了大脑中递归的小人或宇宙中独立心理基础的必要性。 （PsycInfo 数据库记录（c）2026 APA，版权所有。）
